disease: Loose Smut of Wheat and Barley
description: Loose smut is a systemic fungal disease affecting wheat and barley. The fungus infects the developing kernels and replaces them with masses of black spores, which are dispersed by wind during flowering, leading to significant yield losses.
symptoms: Spikelets replaced by black, powdery spores
Affected heads emerge earlier than healthy ones
No vegetative symptoms on leaves or stems
Yield loss proportional to infection rate
favorable_conditions: Cool and moist conditions during flowering
spread: Wind dispersal of spores onto healthy flowers
management: Avoid saving seeds from infected crops
chemical_control: Seed treatment with carboxin, triadimenol, or thiram fungicides
